stem: An 84-year-old client is prescribed diphenhydramine. Which age-related adverse-effect concern is most relevant?

options.A: Older adults are more susceptible to dizziness, sedation, and hypotension from diphenhydramine, so the prescription warrants caution and safety assessment.
options.B: Older adults usually develop less sedation and dizziness from diphenhydramine than younger adults, so age reduces concern about adverse effects.
options.C: Diphenhydramine improves alertness in older adults despite its antihistamine effects, so it is preferred when allergy treatment must avoid drowsiness.
options.D: Diphenhydramine has no age-related precautions for dizziness or blood-pressure effects, so routine geriatric medication review is unnecessary when it is prescribed.

rationale: The current prescription diphenhydramine oral-solution label specifically states that antihistamines are most likely to cause dizziness, sedation, and hypotension in elderly patients. A therefore identifies the label-supported geriatric safety concern. B and D deny the labeled age-related risk, and C contradicts the drug's sedative effects.
educational_objective: Recognize that older adults are especially susceptible to diphenhydramine-related dizziness, sedation, and hypotension and require medication-safety assessment and teaching.

source_original.stem: An 84-year-old client is prescribed diphenhydramine. Which age-related adverse-effect concern is most relevant?

options.A: Older adults are more susceptible to dizziness, sedation, and hypotension from diphenhydramine, so the prescription warrants caution and safety assessment.
options.B: Older adults usually develop less sedation and dizziness from diphenhydramine than younger adults, so age alone reduces concern about adverse effects.
options.C: Diphenhydramine improves alertness in older adults despite its antihistamine effects, so it is preferred when allergy treatment must avoid drowsiness.
options.D: Diphenhydramine has no age-related precautions for dizziness or blood pressure effects, so routine geriatric medication review is unnecessary when this drug is prescribed.

source_original.rationale: Diphenhydramine labeling specifically notes that older adults are more likely to experience dizziness, sedation, and hypotension. Option A accurately identifies those age-related safety concerns. Option B incorrectly claims reduced susceptibility. Option C contradicts diphenhydramine's sedating effect. Option D incorrectly denies the geriatric precautions described in the label.
